checks.topic: Exact predictive and counterfactual state counts
locators: Supplied paper, page 2, Definitions 1-2 and Lemma 3
Supplied paper, page 3, Definition 7 and Theorem 8(i-ii)
checks.conclusion: Correct. A binary history count has t+1 possible values, and all count thresholds recover the count. All coordinate-flip threshold answers recover the full history for t>=3, requiring 2^t states. The constant-history distinction fails at t=2 and the candidate preserves the t>=3 condition.

locators: Supplied paper, page 3, Theorem 8(iii) statement and proof
checks.conclusion: The candidate correctly attributes the bound to the counting proof under joint answer-tuple success. Each retained state can decode the full tuple correctly for at most one history; under uniform histories, m states yield joint success at most m/2^t, so m>=(1-delta)2^t. The wording does not silently promote separate per-query success to joint success.
checks.qualification: The theorem statement uses ambiguous wording about answering every query correctly with high probability; the proof establishes the joint interpretation. This review does not certify the bound under a marginal per-query interpretation.

checks.conclusion: Correct. Third assumes expected squared parameter error for each fixed private input and fixed hard deletion probe, with public/fresh randomness allowed, and obtains a rate-distortion-style information bound. Its loss, averaging and quantifiers differ from the supplied paper joint exact-tuple success probability, so the two numerical bounds are not interchangeable.

locators: empirical_execution/phase10/FINITE_WORD_REVIEW.md, Geometry and access model; Sequential state and canonicality
checks.conclusion: The same stored features feed curation and ridge learning, public-blocker deletions expose private signs, and the exact construction maintains canonical state at the remaining cumulative deletion budget. The wording claims these scoped objects rather than a new general predictive-counterfactual separation; it does not claim the missing thesis lacks them.

checks.conclusion: The six-page supplied manuscript was read, with page 3 also visually inspected. This resolves the prior missing-full-text status for this counterfactual manuscript and permits the stated paper-level comparison. Its validation concerns exact enumeration, algebraic recomputation and falsification checks rather than a benchmark. Dominici remains unavailable; the candidate explicitly leaves that comparison incomplete.

limitations: This approves only the two listed replacements and their evidence status, not complete literature novelty or every argument in the supplied paper.
Theorem 8(iii) is used with its proof-supported joint success event; no per-query probability lower bound is asserted.
No new benchmark, numerical verification suite, inference or original experiment was run.
The supplied third-party full text and page images remain outside the public review.
